entities.label: Ständerat
entities.description: The Ständerat is the upper house of the Swiss Federal Assembly, with representatives elected from the cantons, serving distinct legislative functions alongside the Nationalrat (National Council).<SEP>The Council of States, the second chamber of the Federal Assembly, representing the cantons in the Swiss legislative process with two members per canton.

entities.label: Ständerätin
entities.description: A Ständerätin is a female member of the Ständerat, serving to represent the interests of her canton in the Swiss legislative process.

entities.label: Kanton
entities.description: The term Kanton refers to the administrative divisions of Switzerland, with each representing a region that elects representatives to the Ständerat.<SEP>Kantons are administrative divisions in Switzerland, each possessing unique legal and judicial systems, such as different levels of courts and judicial authorities. They have political autonomy and can regulate certain aspects independently.

entities.label: Nationalrat
entities.description: The Nationalrat is the lower house of the Swiss Federal Assembly, responsible for discussing and voting on legislative proposals, working alongside the Ständerat.<SEP>The National Council, a chamber of the Federal Assembly, composed of representatives elected to represent the Swiss population according to their demographic distribution.

entities.label: Vereinigte Bundesversammlung
entities.description: The Vereinigte Bundesversammlung is a joint assembly of the Nationalrat and the Ständerat, convened for specific legislative purposes, such as elections of federal officials.<SEP>The joint assembly of the two houses of the Federal Assembly of Switzerland, responsible for electing federal judges.

entities.label: Bundesrat
entities.description: The Bundesrat is the federal executive authority of Switzerland, consisting of seven members, each presiding over a department and collectively responsible for the government.<SEP>The Bundesrat is the collective executive body of the Swiss Federal Council, composed of members who oversee various departments and functions within the Swiss government. It does not function as a head of state but is considered the collective head of state of Switzerland.

entities.label: Bundespräsident
entities.description: The Bundespräsident is the president of the Swiss Federal Council, elected annually from among its members to lead the government temporarily but does not serve as a head of state.<SEP>The President of the Swiss Confederation, serving as Primus inter Pares within the Federal Council, representing the council but not acting as a head of state.<SEP>The Bundespräsident is a member of the Bundesrat elected to serve as the President of the Swiss Federal Council for a one-year term, representing Switzerland at ceremonial functions but not holding the powers of a head of state.

entities.label: Landsgemeinde
entities.description: The Landsgemeinde is a traditional assembly held annually in certain Swiss cantons, where citizens directly participate in legislative decisions.

entities.label: Kantonsvertretung
entities.description: Kantonsvertretung refers to the representation concept within the Swiss political system, indicating how cantonal interests are represented, though often deemed misleading in the context of the Ständerat.<SEP>The concept of representation of the cantons in the national parliament, exemplified by the Council of States.

entities.label: Instruktionsverbot
entities.description: Instruktionsverbot is the principle that members of the Ständerat and Nationalrat are not bound by instructions from cantons or political parties during the execution of their mandates, allowing independence in their legislative processes.

entities.label: Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft
entities.description: The Swiss Confederation, operating with a unique system that combines elements of both parliamentary and presidential democracy, known for its directorial system and attributes that distinguish it from other modern democratic models.<SEP>The Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft, known as the Swiss Confederation, is the federal state of Switzerland that governs the country along with its cantonal entities.

entities.label: Föderalismus
entities.description: Federalism in Switzerland, characterized by significant autonomy among the cantons, allowing them to grant their municipalities considerable leeway and involvement in political decision-making.<SEP>Föderalismus refers to the political system in Switzerland that divides authority between the federal government and cantonal governments, emphasizing autonomy and collaboration.

entities.label: Direkte Demokratie
entities.description: Direct democracy in Switzerland, enabling citizens to influence government actions through initiatives and referendums, impacting government activity at various levels.

entities.label: Volksrechte
entities.description: The rights of citizens in Switzerland, rooted in both assembly and ballot democracy, performing functions that include control, initiation, and legitimization of political processes.<SEP>The Volksrechte, or popular rights, represent the rights of citizens to participate in decision-making processes in Switzerland, including various forms of democratic participation such as voting and referendums.

entities.label: Gewaltenteilung
entities.description: The principle of separation of powers in Switzerland, ensuring that the government cannot be dismissed between elections, and the parliament cannot be dissolved by the government.

entities.label: Bundesversammlung
entities.description: The Federal Assembly of Switzerland, consisting of two chambers, the National Council and the Council of States, serving as the Swiss parliament.

entities.label: Schweizer Regierung
entities.description: The Swiss government known as the Federal Council, designed as a collegiate body without a single head of state, emphasizing shared leadership.

entities.label: Staatliche Ebenen
entities.description: The three political levels of Switzerland: Municipality, Canton, and Federation, where districts are part of state administrative structures without independent political authority.

entities.label: Bund
entities.description: The federation encompassing all Swiss cantons, representing the highest political level in Switzerland and possessing overall legislative competence.

entities.label: Parlament
entities.description: The legislative body in Switzerland, referred to as the Federal Assembly, comprised of the National Council and the Council of States, with each serving specific roles in governance.

entities.label: schweizerische Bundesverfassung
entities.description: The Swiss Federal Constitution, which was established in 1848, serves as the fundamental legal document for Switzerland, subject to continuous revision and major renewals in 1874 and 1999.

entities.label: Kantone
entities.description: The cantons of Switzerland, which are semi-autonomous regions playing a crucial role in the federal system and enjoying significant powers of self-government.

entities.label: Bezirke
entities.description: Districts within cantons that serve administrative functions but do not possess political autonomy.

entities.label: Volksvertretung
entities.description: The concept of popular representation within the Swiss political system, exemplified by the National Council as the voice of the citizenry.

entities.label: Interpellation
entities.description: A parliamentary procedure in Switzerland that allows legislators to question government actions and seek clarification.

entities.label: Motion
entities.description: A proposal submitted in parliament to express the opinion or request actions from the government.

entities.label: Postulat
entities.description: A formal request in the Swiss parliament that urges the government to investigate a particular issue or situation.

entities.label: Subsidiarität
entities.description: The principle of subsidiarity in Swiss governance, emphasizing that decisions should be taken at the most local level possible unless they require higher authority.

entities.label: Urnengang
entities.description: The process of voting in Switzerland, particularly in relation to direct democracy mechanisms.

entities.label: Schweizer Demokratie
entities.description: The Swiss democracy is fundamentally representative, involving citizens directly in legislative processes and reflecting a complex relationship between parliamentary and direct democratic elements since its total revision in 1874.

entities.label: Bundesverfassung
entities.description: Bundesverfassung is the Federal Constitution of Switzerland, outlining the country's fundamental laws, including the principles of federalism and the distribution of powers between the canton and the federal level.<SEP>The Bundesverfassung is the Federal Constitution of Switzerland, which is subject to changes that require a popular vote and is primarily determined by the parliament.

entities.label: Volksinitiative
entities.description: The Volksinitiative is a method allowing a certain number of Swiss citizens (100,000) to propose changes to the federal constitution by gathering signatures for a popular vote.<SEP>A procedural method in Switzerland that allows citizens to propose changes to the constitution or legislation, requiring a certain number of signatures for consideration.

entities.label: Referendumsrecht
entities.description: The Referendumsrecht is the right of the populace to challenge parliamentary decisions through a subsequent referendum, where they can either confirm or annul those decisions.

entities.label: Wahlrecht
entities.description: The Wahlrecht is the voting right in Switzerland granting all Swiss citizens aged 18 and above, including those residing abroad, the ability to vote in elections unless disqualified for specific reasons.

entities.label: Stimmrecht
entities.description: The Stimmrecht is the right of eligible voters to vote on local, cantonal, and national proposals, allowing direct participation in the legislative process.

entities.label: Kantonale Rechte
entities.description: The kantonale Rechte refers to the rights of the citizens at the cantonal level in Switzerland, which often surpass those at the federal level, allowing for greater participation in governance.

entities.label: Gesetzesinitiative
entities.description: The Gesetzesinitiative is a method that enables citizens to propose new laws or amendments to existing ones, requiring fewer signatures than constitutional changes, thereby facilitating local governance.

entities.label: Finanzreferendum
entities.description: The Finanzreferendum is a type of referendum concerning the approval of specific financial expenditures, which can be either mandatory or optional based on cantonal regulations.<SEP>A type of referendum related to financial matters in Swiss cantons, which may be optional or mandatory depending on expenditure thresholds defined by cantonal constitutions.

entities.label: Stimmberechtigte
entities.description: The Stimmberechtigte refers to eligible voters in Switzerland who meet the criteria to participate in elections and referendums.

entities.label: Vizepräsident
entities.description: The Vizepräsident is a member of the Bundesrat elected to serve as the Vice President of the Swiss Federal Council for a one-year term, assisting the Bundespräsident in ceremonial duties.

entities.label: Bundeskanzlei
entities.description: The Bundeskanzlei is the Federal Chancellery of Switzerland, responsible for the central coordination and communication between the government, administration, parliament, and the public. It is led by the Bundeskanzler.

entities.label: Bundeskanzler
entities.description: The Bundeskanzler is the head of the Bundeskanzlei, attending all meetings of the Bundesrat without voting rights and overseeing the preparation of council meetings.

entities.label: Guy Parmelin
entities.description: Guy Parmelin is a member of the Bundesrat from the canton of Vaud and serves as the Bundespräsident for 2026.<SEP>Guy Parmelin is a member of the Swiss Federal Council serving as the Federal President in 2026, affiliated with the Swiss People's Party (SVP) from the Waadt (VD) canton, with a background as a master farmer and winemaker.

entities.label: Ignazio Cassis
entities.description: Ignazio Cassis is a member of the Bundesrat from the canton of Ticino and serves as the Vizepräsident for 2026.<SEP>Ignazio Cassis holds the position of Vice President in 2026, representing the FDP from the Tessin (TI) canton. He has a medical background, having served as the former cantonal physician.

entities.label: Karin Keller-Sutter
entities.description: Karin Keller-Sutter is a member of the Bundesrat from the canton of St. Gallen.<SEP>Karin Keller-Sutter is a member of the Swiss Federal Council affiliated with the FDP, serving from the St. Gallen (SG) canton. She has a background as a translator and former government councilor of St. Gallen.

entities.label: Albert Rösti
entities.description: Albert Rösti is a member of the Bundesrat from the canton of Bern.

entities.label: Elisabeth Baume-Schneider
entities.description: Elisabeth Baume-Schneider is a member of the Bundesrat from the canton of Jura.<SEP>Elisabeth Baume-Schneider serves as a member of the Swiss Federal Council, affiliated with the Social Democratic Party (SP) from Jura (JU) canton, with a professional background in social work.

entities.label: Beat Jans
entities.description: Beat Jans is a member of the Bundesrat from the canton of Basel-Stadt.<SEP>Beat Jans is a member of the Swiss Federal Council and represents the Social Democratic Party (SP) from the Basel-Stadt (BS) canton, with expertise in environmental science.

entities.label: Martin Pfister
entities.description: Martin Pfister is a member of the Bundesrat from the canton of Zug.<SEP>Martin Pfister is a member of the Swiss Federal Council representing the party Die Mitte from the Zug (ZG) canton, recognized as a Swiss politician.

entities.label: Regierungsrat
entities.description: The Regierungsrat is the executive body in most German-speaking cantons of Switzerland, functioning similarly to the Bundesrat at the cantonal level.

entities.label: Staatsrat
entities.description: The Staatsrat is the executive body in predominantly French-speaking cantons and the canton of Ticino, analogous to the Bundesrat.

entities.label: Standeskommission
entities.description: The Standeskommission is the executive body in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, serving a similar function as the Bundesrat.

entities.label: Primus inter Pares
entities.description: The Primus inter Pares is a title given to a member of the cantonal executive who leads the government meetings for one year without being termed a governmental leader.

entities.label: Gericht
entities.description: Gericht refers to various types of courts within the Swiss legal system, including first-instance courts, second-instance courts, and specialized courts for different legal matters.

entities.label: Obergericht
entities.description: Obergericht is the term for a second-instance court in many Swiss cantons, responsible for appeals from lower courts.

entities.label: Appellationsgericht
entities.description: Appellationsgericht is a type of appellate court that handles civil law disputes, existing in some cantons such as Basel-Stadt and Ticino.

entities.label: Cour de justice
entities.description: Cour de justice is a type of court specific to the canton of Geneva, responsible for legal adjudications.

entities.label: Zwangsmassnahmengerichte
entities.description: Zwangsmassnahmengerichte are courts responsible for the issuance of coercive measures related to investigations and security detention in various cantons.

entities.label: Verwaltungsgericht
entities.description: Verwaltungsgericht refers to administrative courts that manage public law disputes in larger cantons, distinct from other judicial entities.

entities.label: Spezialverwaltungsgerichte
entities.description: Spezialverwaltungsgerichte are specialized administrative courts for unique legal matters, such as building or tax appeals.

entities.label: Jugendgerichte
entities.description: Jugendgerichte are specialized courts dealing with youth-related legal issues, commonly found across various cantons.

entities.label: Strafgericht
entities.description: Strafgericht specifically refers to courts that address criminal cases in certain cantons, handling serious offenses by replacing district or higher courts.

entities.label: Kassationsgericht
entities.description: Kassationsgericht is a court of cassation that reviewed appeals before its elimination in 2011, formally addressing procedural legal matters.

entities.label: Verfassungsgericht
entities.description: Verfassungsgericht pertains to constitutional courts that some cantons, like Basel-Stadt, Geneva, and Jura, have established to oversee constitutional matters.

entities.label: direkte Demokratie
entities.description: Direkte Demokratie denotes a form of democratic governance where citizens can directly participate in decision-making processes, complemented by representative elements.

entities.label: repräsentative Demokratie
entities.description: Repräsentative Demokratie is a system of governance where elected representatives make decisions on behalf of the citizens, central to the functioning of the Swiss state.

entities.label: Kanton Zürich
entities.description: A geographic region in Switzerland known for its unique political instruments such as the Einzelinitiative, which allows individual initiatives regarding constitutional or legal changes.

entities.label: Kanton Freiburg
entities.description: A canton in western Switzerland, known for its bilingual population and varied cultural heritage.<SEP>A canton in Switzerland that historically maintained a representative democratic government longer than others, until it was replaced by direct-democratic institutions in 1918.

entities.label: Kanton Schaffhausen
entities.description: A canton in northern Switzerland, known for the Rhine Falls and its historic town.<SEP>A canton in Switzerland that recognizes the Volksmotion, which allows a specified number of people to submit a motion to the cantonal parliament.

entities.label: Kanton Solothurn
entities.description: A canton in the northwest of Switzerland, recognized for its historical architecture and natural beauty.<SEP>A canton in Switzerland that has adopted the Volksmotion, enabling a certain number of individuals to submit motions to the cantonal parliament.

entities.label: Kanton Appenzell Innerrhoden
entities.description: A canton in Switzerland, known for its traditional rural culture and direct democracy practices.<SEP>A Swiss canton that recognizes the right of the Einzelinitiative, requiring personal initiatives to be presented to the Landsgemeinde.

entities.label: Kanton Glarus
entities.description: A Swiss canton that also requires personal initiatives to be presented to the Landsgemeinde under the Einzelinitiative system.

entities.label: Kanton Appenzell Ausserrhoden
entities.description: A canton in Switzerland that features the Volksdiskussion, allowing every resident to express their opinion on legislative proposals.

entities.label: Kanton Bern
entities.description: A canton in Switzerland that recognizes the constructive referendum, enabling citizens to introduce alternatives to parliamentary proposals.

entities.label: Kanton Nidwalden
entities.description: A canton in Switzerland that has implemented the constructive referendum since 1996, similar to Kanton Bern.

entities.label: Kanton Basel-Landschaft
entities.description: A Swiss canton that employs a mixed approach to referendums, allowing certain laws passed by a majority in the cantonal parliament to undergo optional referendum.

entities.label: Kantonsrat
entities.description: The cantonal parliament in Switzerland where members can propose various legislative initiatives and motions.

entities.label: Volksabstimmung
entities.description: A form of direct democratic decision-making in Switzerland where citizens vote on specific legislative proposals or changes.

entities.label: Einzelinitiative
entities.description: A procedural method in Switzerland allowing individuals to propose amendments to the constitution or laws, requiring the support of other members.

entities.label: Volksmotion
entities.description: A procedural mechanism enabling a specified number of individuals to submit motions to the cantonal parliament.

entities.label: Volksdiskussion
entities.description: A democratic instrument that allows residents to voice their opinions on legislative proposals before the cantonal parliament.

entities.label: konstruktives Referendum
entities.description: A procedure that allows citizens to propose alternative legislative options for consideration in conjunction with parliamentary proposals.

entities.label: Abstimmungen
entities.description: Periodic voting events where Swiss citizens participate to decide on various political matters.

entities.label: Kantonsverfassungen
entities.description: The constitutions of the cantons in Switzerland that outline the regulations and legal frameworks guiding governance and public participation, including provisions for referendums.

entities.label: Wahlbeteiligung
entities.description: The level of participation of eligible voters in elections and referendums in Switzerland, often measured by the percentage of voters who cast ballots.

entities.label: Schweiz
entities.description: A country in Central Europe known for its mountainous terrain and political neutrality.

entities.label: Lausanne
entities.description: A city in Switzerland, located on the shores of Lake Geneva, known for its educational institutions and as a hub for international organizations.

entities.label: Luzern
entities.description: A city in central Switzerland, known for its preserved medieval architecture and as a gateway to the Swiss Alps.

entities.label: Bellinzona
entities.description: A city in southern Switzerland, known for its medieval castles and as the capital of the canton of Ticino.

entities.label: St. Gallen
entities.description: A city in eastern Switzerland, recognized for its rich history and as the capital of the canton of St. Gallen.

entities.label: Bern
entities.description: The capital city of Switzerland, known for its well-preserved medieval city center and political significance.

entities.label: Zollikofen
entities.description: A municipality in the canton of Bern, situated close to the city of Bern.

entities.label: Kanton Luzern
entities.description: A canton in central Switzerland, noted for its beautiful lakes and mountains.

entities.label: Kanton Tessin
entities.description: A canton in southern Switzerland, known for its Italian-speaking population and Mediterranean climate.

entities.label: Kanton Waadt
entities.description: A canton in western Switzerland, recognized for its wine production and as a center of education.

entities.label: Kanton Basel-Stadt
entities.description: A canton in northwestern Switzerland, home to the city of Basel, known for its cultural institutions and position on the Rhine River.

entities.label: Kanton Uri
entities.description: A canton in central Switzerland, known for its mountainous landscape and traditional tourism.

entities.label: Kanton Thurgau
entities.description: A canton in northeastern Switzerland, known for its agriculture and location along Lake Constance.

entities.label: Eidgenössisches Versicherungsgericht
entities.description: A former federal court in Switzerland, responsible for social insurance cases, now integrated into the Federal Court in Lausanne.

entities.label: Bundesgericht
entities.description: The federal supreme court of Switzerland with jurisdiction over civil and criminal law, located in Lausanne.

entities.label: Bundesstrafgericht
entities.description: The federal criminal court in Switzerland, established to handle serious offenses, located in Bellinzona.

entities.label: Bundesverwaltungsgericht
entities.description: The federal administrative court in Switzerland, responsible for disputes involving federal administration, first located in Bern and later moved to St. Gallen.

entities.label: Bundespatentgericht
entities.description: The federal patent court in Switzerland, established for handling patent disputes, located in St. Gallen.

entities.label: Eidgenössische Schätzungskommission
entities.description: An official federal commission in Switzerland dealing with appraisals, recognized as a federal court.

entities.label: Regierender Landammann
entities.description: The title held by a member of the government of Appenzell Innerrhoden, serving as the head of the cantonal government.

entities.label: Schultheiss
entities.description: A title for the head of government in the Canton of Lucerne up until 2007.

entities.label: Regierungspräsident
entities.description: The title for the rotating president of the cantonal government in Switzerland, assumed for one year.

entities.label: Kanton Baselland
entities.description: The canton of Baselland is neighboring the canton of Basel-Stadt.

entities.label: Appenzell Innerrhoden
entities.description: The Regierender Landammann governs the Canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden.

entities.label: Albert Roesti
entities.description: Albert Roesti serves as a member of the Swiss Federal Council from the SVP, representing the Bern (BE) canton, with a background in agricultural engineering.

entities.label: Schweizerische Volkspartei
entities.description: The Swiss People's Party (SVP) is a major political party in Switzerland that Guy Parmelin represents in the Federal Council.

entities.label: FDP.Die Liberalen
entities.description: The FDP is a political party in Switzerland, officially known as FDP.Die Liberalen, which is represented by both Ignazio Cassis and Karin Keller-Sutter in the Federal Council.

entities.label: Die Mitte
entities.description: Die Mitte is a political party in Switzerland that Martin Pfister represents in the Federal Council.

entities.label: Sozialdemokratische Partei der Schweiz
entities.description: The Social Democratic Party (SP) is a significant political party in Switzerland, represented by both Elisabeth Baume-Schneider and Beat Jans in the Federal Council.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Nationalrat and Ständerat collaborate in the legislative process, convening separately for discussions and jointly in the Vereinigte Bundesversammlung.<SEP>Both the Ständerat and Nationalrat legislate together, treating constitutional amendments and laws that must be approved by both houses.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Ständerat represents the interests of the cantons in the Swiss Federal Assembly, although it does not have direct instructions from them.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Ständerat functions under the concept of Kantonsvertretung, although it is stated that members are not legally obligated to represent their cantons or take instructions from them.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Ständerat operates under the principle of Instruktionsverbot, which ensures that its members maintain autonomy in decision-making, independent of external pressures.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Council of States also constitutes one of the two key chambers within the Swiss parliament.

relationships.label: GOVERNANCE

relationships.label: MEMBERSHIP

relationships.label: RELATION

relationships.label: RELATION

relationships.label: GOVERNANCE

relationships.label: AUTHORIZATION
relationships.description: The Referendumsrecht empowers the Volksrechte by allowing the electorate to challenge and confirm parliamentary decisions.

relationships.label: AUTHORIZATION
relationships.description: The Wahlrecht grants citizens the right to vote, enabling them to exercise their Volksrechte in elections.

relationships.label: AUTHORIZATION

relationships.description: The Federation encompasses the structure and function of the parliament in the Swiss political system.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Swiss Federal Constitution provides the legal structure for the autonomy and governance of the cantons.

relationships.label: MEMBERSHIP
relationships.description: The cantons include districts as part of their administrative organization, though districts lack political autonomy.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The parliamentary procedure of interpellation is used by the popular representation to question the government.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: Motions are adopted by the popular representation to direct actions from the government.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: Postulates are used by the popular representation to request government investigations on specific issues.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Volksinitiative allows citizens to propose changes to the Bundesverfassung, linking citizen initiatives to constitutional alterations.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The process of Volksinitiative is established in the Kantonsverfassungen, allowing citizens to propose constitutional and legal changes.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Finanzreferendum is defined and regulated by the Kantonsverfassungen in Swiss cantons.

relationships.label: GOVERNANCE
relationships.description: The Bundeskanzler leads the Bundeskanzlei, overseeing its functions in the coordination among various government entities.

relationships.label: RELATION

relationships.label: RELATION

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION
relationships.description: The Kanton Zürich enables its citizens to engage with the Kantonsrat through the Einzelinitiative.

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION
relationships.description: Kanton Zürich conducts Volksabstimmungen to determine public opinion on various legislative issues.

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION
relationships.description: The Kanton Freiburg historically had a representative-democratic government that influenced the current structures of the Kantonsrat.

relationships.label: GEOGRAPHY
relationships.description: The Canton of Freiburg is neighboring the Canton of Vaud.

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION
relationships.description: Kanton Nidwalden uses the constructive referendum mechanism similar to Kanton Bern for legislative proposals.

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION
relationships.description: Kanton Basel-Landschaft implements a mixed referendum approach for laws addressed in the Kantonsrat.

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION
relationships.description: The Volksabstimmung process influences decisions made by the Kantonsrat in various cantons.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Volksmotion can lead to actions or decisions taken by the Kantonsrat regarding legislative matters.

relationships.label: REPRESENTATION
relationships.description: The Volksdiskussion allows residents to influence the Kantonsrat through their opinions and discussions.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The konstruktives Referendum can invoke alternate proposals to be considered by the Kantonsrat.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: The Einzelinitiative can trigger a Volksabstimmung if it receives enough support within the Kantonsrat.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: Abstimmungen are similar to Volksabstimmung as both involve public voting on matters of legislation.

relationships.label: RELATION
relationships.description: Wahlbeteiligung is directly related to Abstimmungen as it measures voter participation in these voting events.
